pr_title: Fix check for missing parts on incoming SMS
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

This fixes the issue where longer SMS messages fail to trigger an `sms.incoming_sms` event, as documented in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/105005

I've done some (minimal) refactoring in order to fix it - we no longer use `is_single_part` and `is_multi_part`, but instead do a single check for whether a part seems to be missing. If this is the case, the `break` is still reached, but it's now inside a guard clause instead of an `else` branch. This means the usual case, when `part_is_missing` is false, now happens inside the main loop, without being inside an `if` block. 

The only logic changes concern cases where a single, multipart message is delivered - it now correctly results in an `sms.incoming_sms` event instead of silently ignoring it until a subsequent message arrives.

I have, however, now added two specific test cases concerning the fix here. They both exclusively test `get_and_delete_all_sms`. issue_context.title: Incoming SMS messages over 160 characters do not trigger an incoming_sms event
issue_context.body:
### The problem

This appears to be the same as this issue, marked as stale: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/88001

Shorter messages are delivered without problems, while a 161 character message fails to trigger an event. 

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.11.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

sms

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sms/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
The uploaded logs file includes a little while before a message is sent, then a short message arriving, which results in the following event, taken from developer tools:

event_type: sms.incoming_sms
data:
  phone: "[REDACTED]"
  date: "2023-12-04 15:17:22"
  text: "12345"
origin: LOCAL
time_fired: "2023-12-04T13:17:33.659856+00:00"
context:
  id: 01HGTFM52VWCA6DPV7QN6B11R8
  parent_id: null
  user_id: null

Then a 161 character message arrives, which does not result in any events.
```


### Additional information

I'm hoping to properly investigate this more thoroughly myself, so I'm opening an issue to track the progress/allow anyone else to contribute as necessary.

After observing this issue on my main HA instance, I recreated it in a new Home Assistant OS instance on a Raspberry Pi 4, to ensure that this is still present when nothing else is configured. That is the source of these logs. 

I'm using a USB SIM800C device, which I've been able to use with other software without any problems with longer messages.

I've included the first few loops here, but this continues until I switch logging off.

I've taken this chunk of code https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/7d21ed41a2250bf4f8af22691579927acfb681f3/homeassistant/components/sms/gateway.py#L86-L137 in isolation, and I'm running it outside of Home Assistant, in a Python debugger. 

Stepping through the code, I was initially a bit confused by some of the concepts and variables here, but it seems generally good. 

Based on my first impressions, receiving a single message works as expected.

Receiving a `multi_part` (two, for this test) message needs a bit more attention - `is_multi_part = 0 <= all_parts < start_remaining` is set to `False` when `all_parts` is 2 and `start_remaining` is 2. This means that `all_parts_arrived` ends up being `False`. 

Since `all_parts_arrived` is false, we then hit the `break` on line 128. We never restart the loop, so we never pull in the second message, and the function call ends with no messages having been returned or deleted. 

I think this is a bug, but I'm happy to be corrected if I've missed something important.

I shall keep digging.

Whenever there are two messages, either short then long, long then short, short then short or long then long, it works correctly. I didn't do these tests in HA, but it's pretty simple logic, so I think it should be the same over there. 

My impression is that the branch on line 127 is intended where a message has been broken into parts, some parts are available in the device and some are not yet delivered. In this case, it would make sense to abort the loop and try again once some more have been received. But we're reaching it when there is a multipart message waiting, even if all of the parts are present. 

My suspicion is that line 104 is wrong. It's correct in the multi-message scenarios I listed above, but it's `False` in a single message with nultiple parts scenario, as `all_parts == start_remaining`.

I don't have time to finish this now, but I'll see if I can simulate the "some parts are present and some are missing" scenario, to see if there's a better way to test for it.

After a little more playing, I've simulated the "some parts are present and some are missing" situation.

I propose splitting the check for `is_multi_part` from the "is something missing?" check, that way the code will also be a bit cleaner. If something is missing, a guard clause can still break the loop, but in all other cases we continue through the loop. Fixing the `is_multi_part` logic will fix the underlying issue here, but if we don't handle the "something is missing" case somehow, we'll lose some functionality.

I'll wait a day or so in case anyone objects, then I'll try making the changes and seeing if it works in HA, if it does I'll get a pull request made so the changes can be checked properly.
